setting: You three grew up in Sheffield and all still live in the city, though not close to each other. Your mother died at home on 12 November 2026 after a long illness, and a doctor has already issued the medical certificate. Nobody has registered the death yet, and you're not sure how long you have, which is why Helen has asked the group. You know each other well and have sorted out plenty of family business together before, usually with Helen taking the lead.

Helen.who: 44, woman, the eldest sibling who is taking charge of the paperwork
Helen.knows: You know Daniel is your younger brother, who lives across the city and tends to say he'll sort something and then forget. You know Priya is your youngest sister, who lives in Kelham Island and is the most methodical of the three of you.
Helen.like: You are practical and organised, and you would rather fix a problem than talk about it.
Helen.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when you've found something that needs doing or chasing up.

Daniel.who: 41, man, the middle sibling who is handling the practical side of things
Daniel.knows: You know Helen is your big sister, who always has a plan and sometimes forgets you're not at work. You know Priya is your little sister, who you tease about being the sensible one, and who usually answers the phone when you need her.
Daniel.like: You're easygoing and warm, but you put things off until someone pushes you.
Daniel.texts: You rarely message in this chat unless someone asks you something directly, since your shifts often mean you're asleep when the others are awake.

Priya.who: 38, woman, the youngest sibling who is handling the calls and the forms
Priya.knows: You know Helen is your eldest sister, who has been looking after you since you were small and can be a bit bossy. You know Daniel is your older brother, who is kind but needs chasing, and who you usually end up reminding about things.
Priya.like: You're calm and careful, and you like to get the details right before you say anything.
Priya.texts: You message fairly often, mostly to pass on updates from calls you've made or to ask the others for things you need.

private_lines.Helen: You live in Crookes with your partner, Tom, and work as a pharmacist, mostly on early shifts at a branch near the Royal Hallamshire. Your days are busy and orderly, with a lot of lists, and you usually get home by early evening.
private_lines.Daniel: You live in Hillsborough on your own, and you work nights as a warehouse supervisor at a distribution centre out past Attercliffe. You sleep through the day and have a bit of a routine of walking your dog in the afternoon before you head in.
private_lines.Priya: You live alone in a flat in Kelham Island and teach primary school in Walkley. You're up early for work and your evenings are fairly quiet, with marking and the odd catch-up call with friends.

situation: Siblings sorting out their late mother's paperwork.
topic: How long do you have to register a death in England?

text: How long do you have to register a death in England? Need to know before I start on the rest
checking. i think its 5 days but ill confirm
ok its 5 days from the death, not counting sundays or bank hols. so she died thurs 12th, that was fri 13 as day 1. so its already gone
I know. I counted too. what happens now
gov site says you can still register late, you just have to say why. theres no automatic fine, they can prosecute but thats not normal. they just want the reason written down
im ringing the register office at 9 before class
ok
wait is it 5 days or 5 working days
5 days. sundays dont count. priya says we're late but it's not a big deal
oh
sorry i thought it was ages
rang. they can do appointments but earliest is thurs 26th. they want the MCCD, mums nhs number, her full name and dob, and the informant has to attend with id
she said late is fine just say why when you book
ok thurs works. I'm on till 2 but can get off by 3
they said 4 is the last slot. could we do 3.30. i'll meet you there
yes
dan you there?
yeah. thurs is fine. what do i bring
you dont need to come, helen is informant. she'll need her id, the MCCD, mums nhs number and her birth cert if we can find it
i'll send the full list
sending now
got it. birth cert should be in the box at mine, I'll look tonight
on the dog walk. funeral people rang me, they want the cert before they can book the cremation. they said friday if possible
i said i'd ring back. sorry
they can't have the cert till thurs at earliest, i'll ring them back and explain
you dont need to ring them dan
ok
home. I'll ring the funeral place myself, they'll want the certified copies anyway
how many certified copies do we need btw
at least 3. the bank and the pension people will want their own. i'd say 5 to be safe, theyre £11 each
ok 5
anyone know if we tell the bank before or after the cert
after. tell us once first, it covers most of it
ok
off to work. priya can you do the pension people tmrw, i dont have their number
yes ill do it. the number's in the folder
do we know what time thurs we're meeting at the office
3.30 outside, ill text when im there
ok. going to bed
night
found the birth cert. was in the rent book folder not the box
ill bring it thurs
ok. pension people open at 9 so ringing then
on hold
they need an original or certified copy before they'll do anything. no photos. they can post the form to us once they have it
so we need the 5
ok 5 still
bank says same. they wont do anything till they have the cert but they'll send a form for the rest of the accounts after
on lunch. rang the funeral place
they can do wed 2nd dec if the cert is through by then. otherwise the week after
i said wed
wed is fine
dan can you do wed
just woke up. wed should be ok ill swap with someone
did helen ring them
yes, i said wed
you dont need to ring them dan
ok 👍
walking the dog. do we need to do anything about the flowers or is that the funeral place
funeral place. they said they'd sort the order of service if we send them the names
i'll write the list tonight
home. tom says hi
does anyone know if the bank will want to see her death cert or the actual cert
certified copy. the one from the register office, not the medical one. thats why we need the 5
ok

list of names for the order of service:
mum, mum's sister, the two neighbours, nan's friend from the church, the lady from the choir
is that everyone or did i miss anyone
off to work. add jackie from the club
ok
night
night
